criteria: Documents (c9, c21): one text document per (asset, calendar month) for 2015-01..2020-12 (216 documents) stating asset, month, monthly close-to-close return in percent and last close.

c9 haystack: an InMemoryDocumentStore + InMemoryBM25Retriever Pipeline; for all 216 keyed queries '<ASSET> <YYYY-MM>' the top-1 document's meta (asset, month) equals the query key (pass: 216/216). Negative control: query 'SPY 1999-01' has no matching document, so its top-1 meta must differ from the key (the check can fail). Exit 0.

c14 docling: HTML and CSV files of SPY 2020 month-end closes (12 rows, 3 columns) converted with DocumentConverter; every extracted table cell equals the source cell string (pass: 36/36 data cells plus header per format). Negative control: the same comparison against a copy with one perturbed cell reports exactly 1 mismatch. PDF/OCR paths are out of scope and listed as a limit.

c17 ray-serve: a Serve deployment computes the evaluate.py momentum20 decision (highest positive close[t]/close[t-20]-1, ties alphabetical, else cash) for 40 development decision dates; responses through a DeploymentHandle and through one loopback HTTP request equal the in-process computation (pass: 40/40 and HTTP equal). Negative control: a deliberately wrong lookback (19) disagrees on at least one of the 40 dates, or the control is reported as unable to detect. Ray and Serve are shut down and no ray processes remain.

c18 timesfm: TimesFM 2.5 point forecast of close at step 5 from the 252-session raw-close context for every (fold, asset, decision) key of run-fcmp-merged-r2/forecasts.json (sha256 8829d98c...); predicted r = ln(forecast) - ln(close[t]); keys and targets identical; all forecasts finite. Report per-fold MAE, dev mean and the fcmp paired fold bootstrap (seed 20260923, 10000 draws) against naive and chronos_bolt_small. The comparison is reported, not pass/fail; no superiority claim is preregistered.

c21 sentence-transformers: encode the 216 documents and the 216 keyed queries; embedding dimension 384; two encodes of the documents agree within 1e-5 max abs; report top-1 key accuracy by cosine similarity (measured, not pass/fail) next to the c9 BM25 accuracy.

c24 Qlib: dump the export to Qlib binary format with the tag's dump_bin.py, qlib.init(provider_uri=<temp>, region='us'), and read $close and the expression $close/Ref($close,20)-1 via D.features for SPY, QQQ and IWM over 2015-01-02..2020-12-31; every value equals the pandas computation from the export within 1e-5 relative (float32 storage). Negative control: comparing against a one-session-shifted pandas series reports mismatches.

Outcome: gap 5 is settled only if all six arms meet their pass criteria (so all 15 listed candidates have a retained execution); otherwise advanced, listing what failed. The executions remain run-on-frozen-data evidence, not accuracy or alpha acceptance.

fix_rounds.label: fix round 5 (gap 5 only), written after an independent Codex review of commits 4d82f63..332b0e2 and before any fix-round-5 command ran
fix_rounds.trigger: The review found: (1) the Qlib arm added atol=1e-6 for the momentum expression, so it did not apply the preregistered 1e-5 relative tolerance; (2) the haystack absent-key control cannot fail, TimesFM and MiniLM had no injected negative control, and the Ray expected decisions came from the same helper the deployment used; (3) the Ray cleanup observation (pgrep count 0) and (4) the TimesFM weight size, sha256 and LFS match were not retained as raw files; (5) the Ray attempt-2 listener start time was misquoted.
fix_rounds.change: Rerun into new r5 outputs (r4 outputs stay as they are). (1) Qlib reports mismatches under the preregistered rtol=1e-5 with atol=0 as the criterion of record, and the atol=1e-6 count as a labelled deviation. (2) haystack adds a permuted-meta control (each document's meta rotated by one within the store); its keyed top-1 hits must fall to at most 5 of 216. TimesFM adds an offset-key control (decision index t+1 instead of t) that must make the key/target check fail. MiniLM adds a perturbed-text control (last-close digits changed) whose embeddings must differ by more than 1e-5 from the originals. Ray compares served responses with evaluate.weights(panel, t, 'momentum20') decisions computed in the plan venv with Decimal arithmetic and written, with a sha256, to expected_momentum20.json; the served rule must match 40/40, and the lookback-19 control stays. (3) The Ray run is followed by a retained pgrep count of raylet/gcs_server processes. (4) Retain stat size and sha256 of the TimesFM and MiniLM weight files and the Hugging Face tree API's LFS oid for each. (5) Correct the quoted time from the retained log. The ray run again uses the loopback-only network namespace; docling and the fcmp arms are not rerun.

All 15 listed candidates now have a retained execution on the frozen data.

detection_method: Fix-round-4/5 arms, each with a control that must register a failure (the fix-round-5 controls were added after review found the absent-key haystack query could not fail, TimesFM and MiniLM had no injected control, and Ray's expected values shared the deployment's helper): BM25 keyed top-1 plus a permuted-meta store (2/216 hits); docling cells vs the source strings plus a one-cell perturbed copy (exactly 1 mismatch); Serve responses vs evaluate.weights Decimal decisions plus a lookback-19 rule (4/40 disagreements); Qlib values vs pandas plus a one-session shift (9048 mismatches); TimesFM keys/targets vs the sha256-pinned fcmp file plus an offset-key control (fails); MiniLM repeat-encode drift plus a perturbed-text control (0.0231). Ray cleanup uses pgrep -x with an in-run positive control (1 raylet, 1 gcs_server). Ray loopback was checked from Ray's own session logs (node_ip_address), which is how attempt 2's LAN binding was found. Earlier arms: each fails with a nonzero exit if the library import, pinned version or fit raises; stderr files are retained, all empty. evaluate.verify_inputs checks the plan input hashes before each arm.
remaining: All 15 listed candidates now have a retained execution on the frozen data (c2, c3, c4, c5, c6, c10, c12, c15, c20 in rounds 1-3; c9, c14, c17, c18, c21, c24 in fix round 4). Outcome stays advanced under the preregistered rule: the c9 haystack arm failed its 216/216 keyed-retrieval criterion (182/216), and the c24 Qlib arm failed its rtol-only equality criterion (294 of 9066 values; all within 1e-6 absolute). A redesigned retrieval test (for example a tokenizer or document text without numeric fragments) and a Qlib tolerance suited to float32 storage would each need their own preregistration. These executions show only that each library runs on the frozen data; they are not accuracy, RAG-quality or alpha acceptance.
